_comment: standoff_mm 300 (base distance), depth of field 400 mm, max scan area 500 x 600 mm,
DERIVED from the datasheet, NOT yet applied here (changing them moves every result):
range_mm should be [100, 500] = standoff +- depth_of_field/2 (this file still narrows it to 120/480),
tracker.half_angle_deg should be 25 (back-solved from 10.4 m3 @3.5 m, 28.6 m3 @5.0 m, 49 m3 @6.0 m
-> 25.7 / 25.1 / 24.95 deg; the three agree), this file still carries 30.
STILL PLACEHOLDER, needs a field measurement (each is a 10-30 minute job):
max_incidence_deg - the most sensitive number in the planner. Tilt a flat plate until the data breaks.
body_sphere_r_mm - a handheld head is far bigger than a 45 mm sphere, and the body sits BEHIND the
reference point, not around it. Measure front window -> back, and the max turning radius.
markers_omnidirectional - unverified; if the markers only cover some faces, many poses cannot be tracked.
OPEN, and it changes the coverage baseline by ~2.8x:
the 500 x 600 max area is attained at SOME distance, and the datasheet does not say which.
If it is the far end of the range (500 mm), the area at the 300 mm standoff is only 360 x 300.
Scan a known-size plate at 100 / 300 / 500 mm and measure the point-cloud extents once.

_comment_fov: fov_at_standoff_mm is the datum the footprint scales from; fov_cap_mm stops it growing.
fov_anchor_distance_mm is the distance at which the maximum area is attained - it is the
one number the datasheet does not give. At 300 (= the standoff) the footprint reaches its
cap there, which is the OPTIMISTIC reading and the one the v1 baseline was measured with.
Physically the projected line length grows with distance, so the maximum must sit at the
far end of the range: setting the anchor to 500 makes the footprint at 300 mm only
360 x 300. One flat-plate scan at 100 / 300 / 500 mm settles it, and until then the
anchor is the single knob that moves every result - keep it at 300 to reproduce v1.
Long side vs short side is also unverified: nothing says whether the 600 mm runs along local
x or y, and a 90 deg roll swaps which target samples a pose covers.
_comment_refine: DESIGN, not measured (spec 6.4): the coarse-to-fine pass. After the first
set-cover run, the still-uncovered region is re-aimed on a finer grid than
the target surface was sampled at, because the measured viewpoint count is
limited by candidate generation and not by the selection algorithm.

_comment_acceptance: coverage_target_pct is the SITE's acceptance criterion, not a planner constant:
it buys 'how much area we are willing to patch by hand'. Measured on the real part
(design 2026-10-20, section 6.4), the greedy curve needs ~28 items to reach 99.0% and
~100 to reach 99.7%, so the last 0.7 of a point costs four times the whole rest of
the plan. null runs until the coverage stops growing, which is what reproduces the
validated 102/114 baselines. Override per run with
90.0 since 2026-10-29, down from 99.0. Not a relaxation of the work, a correction of
what is reachable: with the do-not-ride-the-limit policy (robot.joint_span_fraction
= 0.9) the POOL CEILING is 91.19~91.81% on this station, so 99.0 was unattainable by
geometry rather than by algorithm, and every attempt at it either rode the limits or
dropped sweeps. 90.0 asks the connector and the stroke selection to eat essentially
all of the 91.19 ceiling. See docs/tmp/upgrade-plan.md section 11.2 for the full table
of measured ceilings and the original 99.0 figures, which are kept there.
delivery_mode: path = order the sweeps and check a connector between every pair of
delivered points; lean = hand over the poses alone, exactly like v1, promising
nothing about the motion between them. Same coverage either way.
_comment_surface_bias: The one knob for a surface a constant-pose sweep cannot follow for long:
0.0  coverage first  - keep growing into the low-yield tail (min_gain 50, min_stroke 60,
four direction families, cheap ordering, repair may spend 35%)
0.5  shipped         - reproduces the pre-2026-10-22 numbers exactly
1.0  regularity first - stop early (min_gain 600, min_stroke 300, two families, dearer
ordering, repair only 5%), accepting fewer percent on a strongly
curved face in exchange for fewer corners and more parallel bands
The derived values live in SURFACE_ANCHORS in config.py and are written back into the
report under `parameter_provenance.surface_profile`. Writing any of those keys in an
override file wins over the table, and the report says `override` when that happens.
Deliberately NOT derived from the bias: scanner.max_incidence_deg and scanner.range_mm.
Tuning those to buy coverage would make the report look better without the head being
able to scan any of it.
max_points is the hard ceiling on delivered program points. null skips the whole budget
layer, so the selection path is exactly today's.

_comment_stroke: Continuous-path scanning (design 2026-10-19-continuous-scan-stroke-planning-design.md).
A stroke is a straight segment with a CONSTANT pose, and the six coverage conditions are
evaluated at two different steps along it:
coverage_step_mm - the expensive one (every sample in view gets a ray).
check_step_mm - clearance and tracker only (KD tree, and one ray per position).
The coverage step can be coarse BECAUSE BOTH ENDS ARE SAMPLED: the footprint is convex and
about 500 mm long along the motion, so the union of the footprints sampled at positions
closer together than that is exactly the continuous sweep. The design first asked for
50 mm plus a fine re-check of both ends; including the ends makes the re-check unnecessary
and 100 mm still overlaps by 80% - measured, the whole plan was 5.5x the v1 runtime at
50 mm and is inside the 3x budget at 100.
enabled=true is the shipped default: the delivered program is a set of sweeps, so the
coverage figure describes what actually gets scanned rather than a set of stops.
Set it to false to get the v1 pool and result back unchanged (the regression baseline);
max_stroke_mm=0 is the second way of saying the same thing.
overlap_ratio from the design is deliberately absent: it belongs to the G2 grid sweep,
which is not implemented, and a knob nobody reads is worse than no knob.
cost_model / transition_corners_estimate / connector_level / order_axis_weight_mm_per_deg
belong to the point-count work (design 2026-10-20-point-count-reduction-design.md):
cost_model=corners        the selection divides by CORNERS (pose 1+t, stroke 2+t)
instead of by millimetres (pose 100, stroke 900). That ratio
is why the greedy pass took scattered poses and left the
long sweeps for the tail.
cost_model=millimetres    the upstream design's pricing, kept so the two can be
compared on the same part.
connector_level=2         retract + re-orient point between sweeps (today's path)
connector_level=1         spread the rotation over the flight, dropping one corner
connector_level=0         also allow a straight move between two identical poses
(WAIT FOR ROBOGUIDE before turning this on)
connector_level is now the FALLBACK ladder only: with joint_connector on (and the
kinematic gate on) the connector is a single J move and never reaches these routes.
order_axis_weight_mm_per_deg  60 deg of pose change costs the same as 120 mm of
detour. Distance alone makes a large re-orientation look
free, because it is only a short move.
max_prune_rounds 32: the measured run reported '28 -> 28', i.e. pruning was stopped by
the round limit and not by the target. Pruning is pure counting, no rays.
_comment_joint_connector: max_rot_deg_per_mm is 0.669 and that is a MEASURED LOWER BOUND, not a limit: segment
P[11]->P[12] of the delivered X10290.LS turned 173.8 deg over 259.8 mm = 0.669 deg/mm
and the machine flew it. It only constrains the RETRACT fallback routes now, because
the primary connector is a joint move, and a joint move does not have to spread its
rotation over travel - the axis velocities are what carry it.
joint_connector: the connector is one J move from a sweep's end to the next sweep's
start. T_G on the real controller went P[12] -> P[11], a change of band, in one J,
both points reached, no retract corner. This is what removes the retract/reorient
corners, which in the 99% run held ALL SEVEN of the delivered points with no joint
solution while none of the 27 scanning points did.
joint_step_deg: sample resolution for the swept-path clearance check of a joint move.
_comment_motion: type is the DEFAULT motion, and it is L: a scan has to be a straight Cartesian line,
because that line is what the coverage figure was computed from. Points that are only
there to get the head somewhere carry their own per-point motion, and with the
kinematic gate on that is J to a joint-representation point - the only form in which
our choice of joint solution survives to the controller.
CNT0 because that is the site's convention. speed_mm_s is set on the floor and is NOT
joint_speed_ladder is the speed of the J instructions, by how big the move is. A joint
move is where the danger scales with size: J6 sits about 250 mm off the flange axis, so
180 degrees of it swings the scanner through a 400 mm arc, while 5 degrees moves it 22 mm.
Each entry is [largest single-axis change in degrees, speed percent], the last one null
because it is the catch-all. Measured on the 2026-10-30 program (64 points, 50 joint
moves): 20 under 20 deg, 19 between 20 and 60, 11 over 60 - and the 11 were the 7 moves
over 90 deg, the worst being 179.2. Those are the ones this ladder slows down.

_comment_limits: Two sets, on purpose. The planner uses the INTERSECTION and the report says which set
it used. soft = what the controller actually enforces;
mechanical = the datasheet envelope. Never widen soft to pass an acceptance check.
soft is READ OFF the pendant (MENU > SYSTEM > Axis Limit, 2026-10-29), not inferred:
Two of them overturned earlier guesses. J2's roof is +76, not +136. J3's floor is
-120.71, not -185, and that floor is why every F-shoulder pose the planner produced
was unreachable: those solutions sit at J3 near -175, the controller re-expressed them
as -175 + 360 = 185, found that above its +180 roof too, and alarmed MOTN-017
(G:1, A:2,3). The F branch was never available; the old limits said it was.
joint_span_fraction = 0.9 is the do-not-ride-the-limit policy, applied about each
J5 +-112.5, J6 +-324. joint_margin_deg = 5 is applied inside that again. It exists
because J5 = -122 alarmed in ROBOGUIDE while -125 is the documented limit; a pose
3 deg from a limit is not one this machine holds.
_comment_step: max_step_deg is REPORTED, not enforced: the worst joint step between two delivered
points, and the count over this value, go into the kinematics block and the plan is
still delivered. No controller data supports a specific threshold here, and enforcing
an invented one would drop sweeps rather than make them reachable. Treat the count as
a review trigger: import the program and look at those moves.
_comment_wrist_flip: Which wrist branch a delivered solution may use: T (J5 negative), F (J5 positive) or
any. T is the site default, and it is a measurement, not a taste.
A pose has up to eight solutions; the two wrist branches differ ONLY in the sign of
J5, and the pendant calls the negative one T. Two 2026-10-29 experiments settled it:
T_L: 3 points, P1 a joint point at J5 = +106, P2 the same pose as Cartesian with the
constant CONFIG N U T. The controller resolved P2 to J5 = -100.294 and stopped
at the L with MOTN-063 (position configuration mismatch) - an L move cannot
change the wrist branch, so it refused.
T_M: the same program with P2's CONFIG written as the per-point letters N U F.
ROBOGUIDE refused the whole file at load: ASBN-023 Configuration error.
So the letter F is not loadable, and a plan that uses the F branch cannot be flown.
Restricting the planner to T costs very little: the two wrist branches exist as a
pair, so most poses keep one. Set this to 'any' only to inspect the solver.
